content.content:
Fred,

I'm in LA from tomorrow for Dentsu and the Griffin AGM, so can you take over the vendor and partner backlog this week? That's anyone outside the investor work who has an offer, a trial, a quote, terms or an ask in front of us and that one of us has actually engaged with: a call, a reply, a sign-up or paper. Cold pitches nobody answered, including ones we only forwarded around internally, stay off it, and so do the ad networks, PlayableX, Craftsman+ and Singular (they all stay on the UA budget call), the investors, and Mattel, which I'm keeping.

Go by the runway guardrails doc for what we do with each one, plus the one change I posted in #executives on Monday. Anything that needs signing goes the way ESG's note about signing says.

Everyone who is waiting to hear from us should get a written answer this week. Get each company's contact into Contacts so we're not digging through mail next time.

Log it all in a sheet in the Q4 commitments folder, the README in the folder has the columns. Then reply here with what we're keeping and what's waiting on Arthur or me to sign.

Thanks,
Leonard

{"documentId": "f_b98287f6f80fe431a71209", "title": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "name": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "revisionId": "0d3b4ff7c7", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T16:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "text": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments
Leonard, Sep 26. Until we know where the raise lands, this is how we handle anything outside the investor work that wants money, a signature or an answer from us.
How to decide
Go top to bottom and stop at the first one that fits.
1. Already answered. If one of us has already given them an answer, don't write to them again. Note who answered and when. If the answer was "later", it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars too.
2. Cash test. Anything that would cost us cash between Oct 1 and Dec 31 ends now: say no, or cancel it in writing the way their paper or notice asks. A trial or pilot that turns into a paid plan inside that window counts as cash, and so does an offer we would have to take up and pay for before January. Travel and event costs count only when we book them ourselves.
3. Keep. The cash test has one exception: anything on Arthur's keep-running list on our board stays, even if it costs money. Tell them we're staying.
4. Sign. If it costs nothing before January but taking it means someone has to accept terms or sign for the company, it goes the way ESG's note says. Tell them it's with Leonard or Arthur to sign, and with our lawyers first when ESG has to see it.
5. Park. Everything else that's free until January, including offers we could still take up after that. Tell them we'll pick it up in January; it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars (first week of January).
Answers
Everyone who is waiting to hear from us gets a written answer. Portals and no-reply notices don't need one.
"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

content.content:
Hi Leonard,

Following up on our call today, here's how we'd like agreements handled from now on while you're raising:

- Only an officer, you or Arthur, accepts terms or signs for Harmony Games, whatever the amount. That includes click-through terms and portal NDAs.
- Anything with an automatic renewal, exclusivity, a licence of your IP or a term over 12 months comes to us before anyone signs. Send each one to our intake address (it's in your Contacts as ESG Law intake), one email per agreement, so we can open a matter for it.
- Mutual NDAs on our template don't need review, whatever their term. An officer can sign them.

Best,
PERSON_2694_NAME
PARTNER, ESG Law
----

content.content:
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for applying to the Lumencloud Startup Program. Good news, Harmony Games qualifies for $25,000 in Lumencloud credits. The program agreement is attached; it's a 36-month term and the credits start once it's signed. Applications for this cohort close Oct 31.

Aiden
---
Hi Frederick,

Thanks for the call on Wednesday. We'd like to feature Zombie Match 3D in our November puzzle week. The featuring agreement has to be accepted in our partner portal by an authorised signatory of the company. No fees. Could that happen by Oct 24?

Mateo
---
Hi Frederick,

Following our call, the letter of intent is attached: we'd publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea on a revenue share, at no cost to you. It includes 12 months' exclusivity for those markets while we prepare the launch. We'd need it signed by Oct 20.

Noor
---

Hi Frederick,

Heads-up that the free Starter tier on your account ends on Oct 31. If you'd rather drop back to the free plan, reply and I'll downgrade you before then. Free has email alerts only, no paging.

Can you confirm either way?

Dana Whitfield
Customer Success, Pingwise

content.text: Log sheet created in the Q4 commitments folder, and the January review is confirmed for Mon Jan 5, 2026. Writing the 34 rows now.

values: Quote: 12 rigged monster models, $6,400 (50% on kickoff)
Arthur told them we're keeping the art in-house and passing. No new message sent.
Creative retainer proposal, $3,500/month from Oct 1, 3-month minimum; asked us to confirm by Oct 1
No thanks: we're not taking on new paid commitments this quarter, so please don't book the team for October.
ASO retainer proposal, $900/month from Oct 1 (3-month start); asked us to confirm by Oct 1
No thanks: we're not starting new paid retainers this quarter, so please don't send a contract.
Store listing localization quote, 12 languages, $2,640 invoiced on delivery; price holds until Oct 3; waiting on a PO
No thanks: no PO this quarter; we're holding off on new paid work.
Moderated 12-player panel Oct 14, $1,200 prepaid; confirm by Oct 6
No thanks: we won't go ahead with the Oct 14 panel, so please don't recruit for us.
Booth hold, Bay Area Indie Showcase Oct 24: $4,800, $2,400 deposit due Oct 10
No thanks: please release the booth hold; we won't be exhibiting on Oct 24.

UGC Studio pilot (HG-2291) hit its 20-video cap; pilot ends Oct 15 and the Studio plan starts Oct 16 at $1,800/month unless cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io by Oct 15; Priya asked about the next brief
Cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io (Studio plan must not start Oct 16) and told Priya we're not carrying on after the pilot, so no next brief.
Trailer music pack, annual licence, $1,188 paid in full on signature; quote holds until Oct 15; offered to send the licence
No thanks: please don't send the licence; we're not taking on new paid licences this quarter.
Order form for Pro, 4 seats, $149/month from Nov 1; asked for an answer by mid-October
No thanks: please don't set up Pro; we'll stay on the free seat.
Seattle Indie Expo pre-registration push Nov 7; we'd pay travel and hotel for two (about $1,600), booked by Wishwave and invoiced at cost; confirm by Oct 17
No thanks: please don't book any travel for us; partner-booked travel still counts as spend for us this quarter.
30-day trial since Sep 19 moves to Growth at $79/month on Oct 20 unless cancelled by Oct 19 (by email to onboarding contact); Hana offered a walkthrough
Cancelled the trial by email to Hana (no Growth plan on Oct 20) and declined the walkthrough.
November creator campaign, $8,000 with $4,000 deposit on booking; bookings close Oct 31; asked whether to pencil in the slot
No thanks: please don't pencil in the November slot.
Indie showcase slot Dec 5, stand fee $750; asked to set up a call
No thanks: we'll pass on the Dec 5 showcase.
Nightly DB backups move to Standard at $19/month when the plan renews Oct 12; asked us to confirm we want to keep them running
Yes, keep the nightly backups running on Standard from the Oct 12 renewal (on Arthur's keep-running list).
SSL certificate for the game API domain expires Oct 20; renewal $89/year; reply to confirm
Confirmed: please renew/reissue the API domain certificate before Oct 20 (on Arthur's keep-running list).
Night pager / on-call alerting: Starter tier ends Oct 31, account moves to Team at $29/month from Nov 1 unless we downgrade
Staying on Team from Nov 1 so phone and SMS paging keep working; no downgrade (on Arthur's keep-running list).
Publishing LOI for Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea, revenue share, 12 months' exclusivity; signature needed by Oct 20
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first because of the exclusivity, then with Leonard to sign; we'll come back to them on timing against Oct 20.
Startup Program agreement, $25k credits, 36-month term; cohort closes / sign by Oct 31
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first because of the 36-month term, then with Arthur to sign before the Oct 31 close.
Holiday puzzle bundle for Domino Delights, no cost; participation agreement carries an 18-month licence of the game's name, logo and art; sign by Nov 1
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first because of the licence of our IP, then with Leonard to sign; please hold a spot until Nov 1.
Southeast Asia publishing proposal for Domino Delights: 70/30 revenue share, no upfront fee, 2-year exclusive term
It's with our lawyers (ESG) first because of the 2-year exclusive term, then with Leonard to sign if we go ahead.
November puzzle week featuring for Zombie Match 3D, no fees; featuring agreement must be accepted in the partner portal by an authorised signatory by Oct 24
It's with Leonard or Arthur to accept in the portal before Oct 24 (only an officer can accept terms for us).
Mutual NDA on our lawyers' template (2-year term) before the Oct 8 call about the 2026 bundle roadmap
It's with Leonard or Arthur to sign before the Oct 8 call; it's on our lawyers' template so no review needed.
Free brand-monitoring tier; activation needs the click-through terms accepted in the dashboard; asked whether to keep the setup on hold
Please keep the setup on hold: the click-through terms are with Leonard or Arthur to accept (only an officer can accept terms for us).
Font app-embedding licence quote, $640 payable when ordered; valid until Jan 31, 2026
We'll pick it up in January (quote is good to Jan 31).
Trailer voice-over quote, $950 paid when a session is booked; valid until Feb 28, 2026
We'll pick it up in January (quote is good to Feb 28).
Free sample benchmark report; full set is $300/month from February 2026 if we subscribe
Thanks for the sample; we'll pick up the subscription question in January.
$10,000 credits reserved until Feb 28, 2026; asked whether to activate now or later
Later: please keep the credits on hold; we'll pick it up in January.
2026 launch package, $1,200 paid when booked, bookable any time before launch
Not booking yet; we'll pick it up in January.
Pro upgrade proposal, $49/month from the day we upgrade; free plan continues
Staying on the free plan for now; we'll pick up Pro in January.
Free pilot slot in February 2026 for the website demo widget; asked whether to hold it
We'll pick it up in January, before the February slot.
Team trial free until Feb 1, 2026 ($8/user/month after); asked whether to add the rest of the team
Don't add anyone for now; we'll pick it up in January.
Beta free through Jan 31, 2026, paid plans from February; asked for a 30-minute feedback call
Can't do a call right now; we'll pick it up in January.
Startup trial free until Jan 12, 2026, then Growth at $99/month unless cancelled; asked if we'll stay on
We'll decide in January, before the trial ends Jan 12.
Startup promo free until Jan 31, 2026, then $39/month unless cancelled; asked if we'll keep the scheduler
We'll decide in January, before the promo ends Jan 31.

input.subject: Cancellation - workspace HG-2291 (UGC Studio) - do not start Studio plan
input.body:
Hello,

This is Harmony Games' written notice that we are cancelling before the Studio plan starts on workspace HG-2291 (Clipforge UGC Studio).

Please do not start the Studio plan on Oct 16, 2025 and do not bill us the $1,800/month. The pilot can end as scheduled on Oct 15, 2025.

Please confirm the cancellation in writing.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games
frederick.stone@harmonygames.co

Thanks to you and the team for the work on the pilot.

Best,
Frederick

Best,
Frederick

input.body:
Leonard,

The backlog is done. All 34 companies are in "Q4 commitments log" in the Q4 commitments folder (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/4936eceb9ac25927/edit). Everyone who was waiting on us has a written answer, and each company's contact is in Contacts.

What we're keeping (Arthur's keep-running list):
- Vaultline: nightly DB backups move to Standard, $19/month from the Oct 12 renewal
- Certwell: API domain SSL renewal, $89/year, due Oct 20
- Pingwise (the night pager): Team plan, $29/month from Nov 1

Waiting on you or Arthur to sign (all on the founders' board To Do list):
- Playfuse: mutual NDA on ESG's template, so no review needed. You or Arthur, by Oct 8 (before their call).
- Orbit Store: November featuring agreement, accepted in their portal. No fees. You or Arthur, by Oct 24.
- Markward: click-through terms for the free brand-monitoring tier. You or Arthur, no deadline.
- Kinetic Arcade: Japan/Korea publishing LOI with 12 months' exclusivity. ESG first, then you, by Oct 20.
- Lumencloud: $25k credits program, 36-month term. ESG first, then Arthur, by Oct 31.
- Bundlehouse: holiday bundle agreement with an 18-month licence of Domino Delights' name and art. ESG first, then you, by Nov 1.
- Lanternfly Publishing: Southeast Asia deal for Domino Delights, 2-year exclusive. ESG first, then you. No date; I've asked them for the full draft.
The four ESG ones each went to ESG Law intake as separate emails today, with the checklist details.

Also:
- Ended under the cash test (12): Brightlane, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor Events, Soundvault, Framewell, Wishwave, Streamcast Talent, Spotlight Fest. Plus two trials that were about to turn paid: Clipforge (cancelled in writing to Paylane billing before the $1,800/month Studio plan starts Oct 16) and Reviewly (cancelled before $79/month starts Oct 20). Wishwave was the partner-booked travel your Monday change covers.
- Parked for the Jan 5 review (11): Glyphworks, Driftwood Audio, Benchmarkly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam, Echohall, Tilecast, Loopnote, Quillcraft, Retainly, Hootline.
- Already answered: Motive Forge (Arthur passed on Sep 19).
- Nova Rewards withdrew their offer on Sep 23, so they're not on the log.

Fred

content.text:
I've worked through the whole vendor and partner backlog and replied to Leonard on his email. That's 34 companies, each decided using the guardrails doc plus the change he posted in #executives on Monday: travel a partner books and bills us now counts as spending.

**What we're keeping (from Arthur's keep-running list):**
- **Vaultline:** database backups, $19/month from Oct 12
- **Certwell:** SSL certificate, $89, due Oct 20
- **Pingwise:** the night pager, $29/month from Nov 1

**Waiting on Leonard or Arthur to sign (7 cards on the Harmony Games board's To Do list):**

| Company | What | Our lawyers (ESG) first? | Who signs | Needed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Playfuse | Mutual NDA on ESG's template | No | Leonard or Arthur | Oct 8 |
| Orbit Store | Featuring agreement, accepted in their portal | No | Leonard or Arthur | Oct 24 |
| Markward | Click-through terms for the free tier | No | Leonard or Arthur | No date |
| Kinetic Arcade | Publishing letter of intent, 12 months' exclusivity | Yes | Leonard | Oct 20 |
| Lumencloud | $25k credits, 36-month term | Yes | Arthur | Oct 31 |
| Bundlehouse | Agreement licensing Domino Delights' name and art for 18 months | Yes | Leonard | Nov 1 |
| Lanternfly Publishing | 2-year exclusive deal | Yes | Leonard | No date |

The four that go to ESG each went to ESG's intake address as a separate email today, with their checklist details. Those emails say I'll send the documents over, but I didn't attach them. Someone needs to send ESG the files from the Vendor & partner paperwork folder in Drive.

**Everything else:**
- **Ended (12):** said no to 10 companies whose offers would cost money this quarter. I also cancelled two trials that were about to turn paid:
  - **Clipforge:** your tracker sheet says the pilot is free until Jan 15. But the pilot agreement says it ends early once the 20-video cap is hit, and you've hit it. So the $1,800/month plan would have started Oct 16. I cancelled in writing to their billing address, Paylane, as the notice requires.
  - **Reviewly:** would have become $79/month on Oct 20; I cancelled by email to Hana there.
- **Parked for the Jan 5 review (11):** each was told we'll pick it up in January, and each has its own all-day reminder on your calendar that day.
- **Already answered:** Arthur turned down Motive Forge on Sep 19, so I didn't write to them again.
- **Left off the log:** Nova Rewards, because they withdrew their offer on Sep 23.

All 33 companies that were waiting have a written answer. I added 31 contacts to Contacts with the company in the job field; the other three were already there. The log, "Q4 commitments log", is in your Q4 commitments folder and shared with Leonard.

Things to watch for: confirmations from Paylane and Reviewly, and the full draft agreement I asked Lanternfly for so ESG has something real to review.
